newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical union offers deal in pay talks.
newsitem.headline: German chemical union offers deal in pay talks.

text.p: Germany's IG Chemie trade union said on Wednesday it had offered employers what it called a compromise package in chemical industry negotiations over the 1997 pay round.
Wage negotiations had broken down overnight on the issue of sick pay entitlements, which a law passed in October allows companies to cut from 100 percent of salary to 80 percent.

Sources close to the talks said the chemical employers had been prepared to continue with full sick payments as long as individuals with high absenteeism rates were penalised in other areas, such as traditionally generous Christmas bonuses.
IG Chemie, meanwhile, wanted any impact on bonuses to reflect the absenteeism of a company's whole workforce rather than individuals.

But just after talks restarted on Wednesday morning, IG Chemie chief negotiator Hans Terbrack said the union had now offered a deal under which absenteeism penalties would be based on a combination of individual and company sickness levels.
He added that negotiators for the BAVC chemical industry employers federation were now discussing the proposal.
Negotiations for the 1997 wage claim, which would normally be held next spring, had been brought forward because of strong resistance by workers to the new sick-pay law.
Two earlier rounds of talks for the 590,000 workers in the industry have already collapsed on the issue of sick pay.

Sick pay is, however, only one issue on which agreement must be reached. IG Chemie has already rejected an offer by employers of a 2.5 percent wage rise as "completely unacceptable", demanding a 4.2 percent increase.
